content.thinking:
I'm going through the claims one by one now. The root cause looks like the cached entries stopped picking up new purchases from A5, so they fell behind the ledger, which stayed correct. I'm checking that against the evidence references and it's backed by AL1 and T5, T11, and T13. The plain-words explanation is hedged, so I'm weighing it against F1 and AL1 to see how far it holds.

Next I'm checking the symptom and causal chain against the evidence: the account pages were serving copies missing at most one purchase, and the oldest purchase no stale figure counted was recorded at that point. The code-fix claim holds because the entry was compared with the account it rendered, using the purchase count. Nothing I've read shows anyone watching whether the updates kept up.

I'm working through the rest of the claims: the alert wasn't linked to the on-call incident, so nobody was paged, and the discarding step didn't touch the cache's updates. The mitigation only cleared entries that disagreed at check time, and nothing I've read shows the updates were restarted.

I'm confirming that the last claim holds: the discarding only covered the stale figures, which the evidence shows was the whole of the problem.

supported.quote: The cached spend entries in io-summary-cache stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}, so they fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct.
The evidence read does not show why the updates stopped.

these copies stopped being updated with new purchases for a reason the record does not show; account pages kept showing the out-of-date copies, likely because a page did not check a copy against the shopper's purchases before showing it.

Cached spend figures that were not on the discarded list, and any that went stale later, could keep showing shoppers totals that leave out their latest purchases, and more would go stale each time a shopper bought again.
Account pages showed shoppers spend totals missing their latest purchases
Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that left out purchases they had made. The purchases themselves were recorded correctly.

The pages were serving cached copies of the spend figures from io-summary-cache that had fallen behind the purchase ledger, while the ledger itself stayed correct. These stale cached copies were the whole of what was wrong.
The cached copies stopped taking in new purchases from {A5}. The oldest purchase that no stale figure counted was recorded then.
What stopped the updates is not shown: the Investigator Agent got back no metrics and no log lines for the service.

In it, the account page's `_the_figure_for` serves any entry the cache returns without comparing the entry's purchase count with the purchases the page has already loaded for that account. So a stale entry kept being served for as long as the cache could be reached.

Nothing was seen watching whether io-summary-cache's updates kept up with the purchase ledger. The copies stopped keeping up at {A5}, and the only thing that found it was the stale-figure check, once stale figures were being served.
The CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: which the discarding of entries did not touch
No per-minute metrics and no log lines came back for the service when the Investigator Agent asked for them.
rather than only clearing the entries that were stale at that moment
The alert named each stale entry and pointed to a safe fallback: the purchase ledger, which never moved.
The mitigation discarded only the entries that disagreed when the alert's check ran. Nothing seen restarted the cache's updates, so the copies were left free to go stale again.
